label: Rumi
note: Raw milk, no starter; the name means Roman, but it is Egyptian.

about.text: The main hard cheese of Egypt, made from full-cream cow's or buffalo milk without starter and ripened for several months, when it turns sharp and pungent.

how.text: A hard, crumbly, salty Egyptian cheese of the pecorino/manchego family, made from raw milk without starter.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: With rennet, calf or microbial; the source names no standard coagulant.
Glycolysis, lipolysis and proteolysis give an open texture and a sharp, pungent flavour after 3–4 months.

Egypt's main hard cheese; ripens 3-4 months, sold as 10 kg discs, coagulation method not documented, rennet assumed

facts.v: The one Egyptian cheese exempt from the pasteurised-milk rule, since pasteurised milk does not give its flavour
